bull_bear.body: highly confident, transformational, and disciplined; management emphasizes sustainability over margin expansion, highlights portfolio shift from volume to value, and frames oncology/vaccines as future growth engines; tone is strategic, data-driven, and investor-aligned
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Shingrix’s CVMD linkage is a unique commercial differentiator — not just a vaccine but a preventive cardiology tool; oncology field force is tiny (25 KAS) but highly targeted (1,000 oncologists), enabling high ROI despite low headcount; digital touchpoints (4M/quarter) now complement and extend field force, reducing need for large-scale MR expansion
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The deck states a 'sustained focus to strengthen and optimize the balance sheet'.
- PAT for the quarter was helped by a one-off dividend from Biddle Sawyer Limited, described as a 100% subsidiary.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Strong portfolio of flagship, HCP-endorsed brands (Augmentin, Calpol, Ceftum, Betnovate, Neosporin, T-bact, Tenovate, Boostrix, Infanrix Hexa, Varilrix, Havrix) underpinning market leadership in Private Vaccines, Anti-Infectives and Dermatology
- Global scale and expertise as a subsidiary of GSK plc, benefiting from parent-group resources and R&D
- Robust and integrated omnichannel marketing ecosystem combining in-person HCP engagement with digital platforms (webinars, podcasts, virtual learning)
- Digital-led innovation ecosystem integrating AI, machine learning and advanced data analytics (Minerva, GiGi, Rep Copilot) into commercial operations
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Tariff and trade-policy uncertainty in major markets — Governments, particularly in the US and EU, are prioritising domestic drug manufacturing and supply-chain localisation amid tariff uncertainty and trade tensions, creating policy risk for the globally integrated biopharma supply chains GSK's India operations are part of.
- Persistent pricing pressure on medicines — Despite governments viewing biopharma as a key growth engine, growing pressure on drug pricing continues across major markets, a structural constraint on industry margins.
- Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) / antibiotic-stewardship exposure — As a large manufacturer of antibiotics, the Company faces regulatory and reputational risk tied to AMR; its global strategy commits to certifying all internal antibiotic-manufacturing sites by end of 2026, with the Nashik site newly awarded the BSI Kitemark for seven antimicrobial products, subject to annual surveillance audits to retain certification.
- Data-privacy and marketing-conduct regulatory compliance — The Company is preparing for operationalisation of India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules, 2025, requiring strengthened data-privacy/security governance, alongside continued compliance with the Uniform Code of Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (UCPMP) 2024.
- Third-party / vendor dependency — A Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) process is applied during vendor onboarding, indicating reliance on and exposure to external vendors and supply partners.
- Dependence on parent-level (GSK plc) risk and control frameworks — The Company's Internal Control Framework, Independent Business Monitoring and Management Monitoring exercises are approved/designed by the Global GSK Leadership Team and the Global Risk Oversight and Compliance Council (ROCC), reflecting structural dependence on group-level governance for local risk oversight.

business.body: GenMeds: +9% market growth, brands Augmentin/Ceftum/T-Bact grew double digits; Vaccines: +11% YoY, led by Boostrix/Varilrix/Havrix; Shingrix: ~INR75cr annual run rate (CY25), 80% growth YoY, now tied to CVMD strategy; Specialty: Zejula/Jemperli launched in Q3, first full quarter with 250+ patients on therapy; Jemperli gained first-line endometrial cancer approval in Dec 2025, expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; pipeline includes Belantamab (multiple myeloma), Bepirovirsen (chronic Hep B functional cure), RSV vaccine, Efimosfermin (liver disease)

business.body:
- The deck says the GSK portfolio (all Gen Med and Vaccine brands except the GoA portfolio and discontinued brands) 'has maintained its leadership with 23% share in rep market', with GSK's rep market growing 10% versus GSK portfolio growth of 11% (Price 2.4%, Vol 4.4%, NI 1.8%).
- Segment leadership is claimed on both sides of the portfolio: Gen Med portfolio 'maintained its leadership with 22% share in rep market' (rep market 9% vs GSK 11%) and the Vaccines portfolio 'maintained its leadership with 27% share in rep market' — though for Vx the deck shows the rep market at 20% against the GSK Vx portfolio at 14%.
- Established Vaccines is described as continuing to lead the overall Vx market with 26.1% Value market share (MAT), at Unit EI 95 and Val EI 93; the deck states Paediatric Vaccines 'continued leadership in the self pay private pediatric market'.
- Individual brands are shown holding large shares of their own markets in Q1 FY27: T-Bact 57.5% (+2.6%), Calpol 31.2% (+1.6%), Ceftum 32.7% (+0.2%) and Augmentin 22% (+1.0%), with Key Promoted Brands at 23.4% (0%).
- GSK's growth is said to have outgrown the market in metro class and specialties, while the deck notes GPs 'continue to dominate with 40% Rxns volume and growth faster than Specialty and Super specialty Rxns'.

- [Market context] The deck reports IPM grew 13.5% in Q1 FY27 and separately shows IPM growth of 13.6% for Apr-May'26 attributed largely to price (Volume 8.7%, NI 1.9%, Price 3.0% are the components shown); chronic (40% of industry, 15% growth) grew better than acute (60%, 11%) and MNCs (16% share, 17% growth) grew ahead of Indian players (84% share, 13%).

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Oncology: Belantamab (Blenrep) launch expected in FY27; liver disease: Bepirovirsen (first functional cure for Hep B) and Efimosfermin in pipeline; RSV vaccine nearing approval; 12-15 indications for next-gen ADC B3H7 over 5 years; oncology indications expanding to rectal cancer (2026 readout)
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Sustaining General Medicines as the revenue backbone (>80% of revenue) through continued high-quality scientific engagement, HCP endorsement and digital enablement
- Scaling Specialty Medicines (Oncology and Respiratory) as the next frontier for precision-led growth, supported by a Patient Support Programme and CARE accounts to improve access, adherence and outcomes
- Strengthening the adult vaccination ecosystem, recalibrating strategy to focus on cardiovascular-and-metabolic-disease (CVMD) risk cohorts for shingles prevention, and closing gaps in maternal and second-year childhood immunisation
- Building a robust and diversified supply chain via stronger contingency planning, alternate manufacturing options and improved end-to-end visibility, following FY2025-26 supply disruptions that had a material impact on performance
- Accelerating the innovation pipeline across Oncology, Vaccines and liver disease management through new launches and clinical trial participation
- Driving digital-first, AI-enabled commercial operations (Minerva, GiGi, Rep Copilot) to improve field effectiveness and HCP engagement
- Building a performance-led culture through structured succession planning, high-potential talent identification and technology-enabled leadership development
- Contributing to India's Viksit Bharat @2047 mission by investing in next-generation therapies, new access models and digital enablement
- Company maintains a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (approved 27th October 2016) and recommends dividends annually to Members, subject to AGM approval; a Rs. 57 per equity share final dividend was recommended for FY2025-26, to be voted on at the 101st AGM on 30th June 2026. As part of its oversight function, the Board reviews the strategy, annual business plan and capital expenditure budgets.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY2025-26 marked GSK's foray into Oncology in India with the launch of Jemperli (dostarlimab) and Zejula (niraparib), including launch engagements across 50+ centres, the introduction of the Phoenix Patient Support Programme, and access expansion through CARE ecosystems (CGHS, ECHS, ESIC). On Vaccines, the Company scaled its digital ordering platform VaxiKart (12,000+ HCPs onboarded, now ~45% of paediatric vaccine revenues) and its 7-Star Awareness Campaign across 3,000+ paediatric clinics, and is exploring new adult-vaccination access channels via hospital partnerships, armed forces and railways. At the Nashik manufacturing site, the Company installed a 300 kW solar power system, a 66 KLD sewerage treatment plant for domestic wastewater treatment, and a 900 TR advanced cooling tower, and upgraded the electrical/control panel on the Alexander Werk Roll Compactor used in Albendazole manufacturing and added electronic data integration for in-process quality-check instruments at Eltroxin manufacturing.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global medicine market expected to grow at 5-8% CAGR to reach about USD 2.4 Trillion by 2029, with specialty medicines rising to ~46% of global spending by 2029 from 27% in 2014
- Rising chronic illness (cancer, chronic respiratory disease, neurological illness) projected to account for the top ten global disease burdens by 2032, keeping oncology a top biopharma innovation priority alongside new technologies such as antibody drug conjugates
- Growing risk from infectious disease, vaccine-preventable outbreaks and antimicrobial resistance is accelerating the industry-wide shift toward preventive healthcare
- Advances in AI and automation are expected to improve R&D and manufacturing efficiency across biopharma in the near-to-medium term
- India's economy remained resilient in FY2025-26 on tax reforms, GST rationalisation, infrastructure spending and new Free Trade Agreements with the UK and EU, with IMF projecting India GDP growth of 6.5% in 2026 and 2027
- Indian pharmaceutical industry evolving from manufacturing hub to global innovation hub, with the domestic market projected to grow from ~USD 60 Billion to ~USD 130 Billion by 2030
- Structural demand tailwinds: India's population aged 50+ projected to rise from 193 million (2011) to 404 million by 2036, alongside rising life expectancy and disease burden
- Expanding healthcare access and affordability via government schemes (Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY covering 120 million families) and digital health infrastructure investment (Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, National Biopharma Mission)
- Union Budget 2026-27 repositions biopharma/biologics as a core national pillar, including a Rs. 100 Billion Biopharma SHAKTI outlay, 1,000+ accredited clinical trial sites, customs duty exemption on 17 cancer drugs, and Rs. 47,700 million for the PM-ABHIM health infrastructure mission
- 26 ongoing and planned global and local clinical trials being conducted in India, including trials for Bepirovirsen, an investigational antisense oligonucleotide targeting a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B
- Jemperli progressing through approval for expanded indications across other solid tumours, following first-line approval for primary advanced and recurrent endometrial cancer
- Pipeline acceleration underway in Oncology, Vaccines and liver disease management, including the upcoming Blenrep (belantamab mafodotin) launch in haemato-oncology and the entry of Arexvy (RSV vaccine for older/high-risk adults)
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: GSK India delivered its first INR1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, driven by supply normalization in GenMeds and strong oncology vaccine launches, with EBITDA margin expanding to 35.9% — the key change is the transition from volume-driven generics to high-margin specialty assets like Zejula/Jemperli and Shingrix, which now define future growth and margin sustainability.

open.item: Directors recommended a final dividend of Rs. 57 per equity share for FY2025-26, subject to Member approval at the AGM on 30th June 2026, absorbing Rs. 966 crores, payable on or after 1st July 2026.
Company will significantly scale up investments in Oncology over the next few years towards its mission of a cancer-free India.
Company is preparing to enter the haemato-oncology space with the launch of Blenrep (belantamab mafodotin) for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.
Entry of Arexvy, a vaccine to prevent lower respiratory tract disease caused by RSV in older adults and high-risk populations, to further strengthen the vaccines portfolio.
26 ongoing and planned global and local clinical trials being conducted in India, including trials for Bepirovirsen aimed at a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B.

Following FY2025-26 supply chain disruptions that materially impacted performance, Company is investing in stronger contingency planning, alternate manufacturing options and improved end-to-end visibility to safeguard business continuity.
Jemperli is progressing through approval for expanded indications across other solid tumours, beyond its first-line approval for primary advanced and recurrent endometrial cancer.
Company recalibrated its Shingrix strategy to focus on patient cohorts with cardiovascular and metabolic disease (CVMD) conditions, recognising their higher shingles risk.
Company accelerated efforts to bridge gaps in maternal and second-year childhood vaccination through integrated engagement and direct parent education.

Company is exploring additional access channels for adult vaccination through collaborations with private hospitals, armed forces and railways, alongside joint business partnerships with strategic hospital partners to expand institutional access.
